subject: Startups
title: PayPal's Cash Incentive
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on PayPal's Cash Incentive.

hook.text: PayPal paid people to sign up. Literally. $10 for you, $10 for your friend. It sounds insane, but it worked.

buildup.text: At its peak, PayPal spent $60-70 million on referral bonuses. Investors were terrified of the burn rate.

discovery.text: But each new user increased the network's value. More users meant more merchants, more trust, more transactions.

twist.text: PayPal gradually reduced the bonus from $10 to $5 to $0 as network effects took over and growth became organic.

climax.text: The strategy worked: PayPal reached 5 million users by early 2000. eBay bought it for $1.5 billion in 2002.

punchline.text: Sometimes the best growth hack is cold, hard cash.

quiz.question: How much did PayPal initially pay per referral sign-up?
